The Lifting Supervisor is responsible for overseeing and coordinating all lifting operations on site. This includes planning and preparing lifting activities involving tower cranes, mobile cranes, boom trucks, forklifts, gantry cranes, and related equipment. The role ensures all lifting tasks are performed safely, efficiently, and in full compliance with project requirements and regulatory standards. The Lifting Supervisor leads the lifting team and works closely with rigging personnel to assess conditions and guide proper execution of all lifting operations. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Health & Safety Responsibilities 
 Ensure all lifting equipment and materials are maintained in safe, operable condition, with all safety devices functional, calibrated, and properly certified.
 Enforce best practices in rigging and lifting techniques among all personnel.
 Maintain a consistently high standard of safety across all lifting activities.
 Verify that all required permits, documentation, and approvals are in place before lifting operations begin.
 Ensure all lifting equipment and devices comply with applicable Canadian standards and regulations in Ontario.
 Operational Responsibilities 
 Plan and prepare upcoming lifting activities, including equipment allocation, material requirements, task scheduling, and team dispatch in alignment with site priorities.
 Establish and implement clear procedures to ensure full understanding of lifting operations among lifting and logistics teams.
 Develop and enforce pre-start briefings and equipment-specific checklists for each type of machinery.
 Confirm that all operators and drivers complete required pre-shift equipment inspections.
 Conduct regular inspections of lifting devices to verify condition and readiness before each shift.
 Coordinate and organize lifting activities across all sites, ensuring efficient daily operation of lifting teams.
 Closely monitor the installation and operation of major equipment such as tower cranes, crawler cranes, and overhead cranes.
 Review and ensure strict adherence to approved lifting plans.
 Support equipment tracking and documentation of all Ontario Transit Group lifting devices.
 Maintain smooth team operations through proper planning of staffing, shift scheduling, and coverage.
 Collaborate closely with site engineers to ensure alignment of lifting activities with overall project goals.
 Perform daily on-site rounds to monitor team performance and provide coaching to improve skills.
 Adapt tasks and responsibilities as required throughout the duration of the project.
 Reporting Responsibilities 
 Ensure daily pre-start reports are completed and uploaded to the designated server.
 Collect and submit daily reports from site teams, including personnel attendance, hours worked, and tasks completed.
 Record hourly meters and/or kilometers of all on-site equipment (e.g., mobile cranes, heavy equipment) and provide updates to the Plant Engineer.
 Confirm that all lifting devices and equipment inspections are completed daily and forwarded to the Lifting Manager.
Minimum of 10+ years of experience within a construction-based Lifting Department, demonstrating a foundational understanding of lifting operations, site procedures, and safe equipment handling. Candidates with additional hands‑on exposure in heavy civil, industrial, or infrastructure projects will be considered an asset.
 Strong and up‑to‑date knowledge of lifting standards, regulations, and best practices, including safe rigging methods, equipment limitations, and compliance requirements relevant to construction environments.
 Valid Appointed Person Certification, confirming the ability to plan, supervise, and manage lifting operations while ensuring adherence to all safety protocols and legislative requirements.
 Proficiency in plant and logistics operations, including coordinating equipment movement, supporting site logistics planning, and ensuring efficient use of lifting assets across multiple work fronts.
 Demonstrated engineering and supervisory abilities, with the capacity to interpret technical documentation, review lifting plans, and oversee teams executing lifting and rigging tasks safely and effectively.
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, enabling clear direction to crews, coordination with site management, and effective collaboration with engineering, logistics, and HSE departments.
 Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and Outlook, with the ability to prepare reports, maintain equipment records, track documentation, and support daily operational administration.

Job Description Summary 
Le/la PMCC Senior est un(e) expert(e) en gestion contractuelle, financière et des achats dans le domaine de la Construction et Mise en service (C&C). Fort(e) d'une solide expérience sur des projets industriels et énergétiques complexes, il/elle agit comme mentor et référent métier auprès des PMCC, en apportant des conseils stratégiques, en partageant les meilleures pratiques et en favorisant leur développement professionnel. Ce rôle ne comporte aucune responsabilité hiérarchique ou opérationnelle directe sur les autres PMCC, qui conservent l'entière responsabilité de leurs projets et décisions.
The Senior PMCC is an experienced professional in contractual, financial, and procurement management within Construction & Commissioning (C&C). With extensive experience in complex industrial and energy projects, the Senior PMCC serves as a mentor and subject matter expert, providing strategic guidance, sharing best practices, and supporting the professional development of other PMCCs. This role carries no direct managerial or operational responsibility for other PMCCs, who retain full accountability for their projects and decisions. 
 Job Description 
 Responsabilités principales
 1. Contrat et réclamations
 Agir comme expert de référence en gestion contractuelle, notamment sur les périmètres, exclusions, avenants et réclamations.
 Conseiller les PMCC sur les écarts contractuels et les stratégies de préparation des réclamations client.
 Partager les meilleures pratiques en matière de collecte de preuves, d'imputation des coûts et de documentation contractuelle.
 Apporter un soutien consultatif sur les situations contractuelles complexes, en collaboration avec les Directeurs de Projet et les Contract Managers.
 2. Budget et contrôle des coûts
 Fournir une expertise et des conseils sur le contrôle des budgets chantier, les prévisions financières et la distribution des coûts.
 Accompagner les PMCC dans l'identification des risques financiers, des écarts budgétaires et des mesures d'atténuation.
 Partager les meilleures pratiques pour la préparation des revues mensuelles (MPR/PMR).
 Contribuer à l'amélioration des méthodes et outils de suivi budgétaire.
 3. Achats et sous-traitants
 Conseiller les PMCC sur les stratégies d'achat, les appels d'offres (RFQ), les négociations et la gestion des contrats de sous-traitance.
 Partager son expertise sur l'élaboration des SoW, les bons de commande (PO), la facturation et les processus VBB.
 Promouvoir l'alignement contractuel des sous-traitants avec les priorités SQDC de GEV, y compris les exigences EHS.
 Accompagner les PMCC dans la résolution de problématiques complexes liées aux achats et aux sous-traitants.
 4. Avant l'ouverture du site et mobilisation
 Fournir des conseils sur la préparation des Gate Reviews et les processus de mobilisation conformément aux standards GEV.
 Partager les meilleures pratiques concernant les budgets de mobilisation, la planification et la préparation des chantiers.
 Apporter une expertise sur les stratégies logistiques, les installations de chantier et les besoins en outillage (achat ou location).
 Conseiller sur la coordination des équipes, du TFA et des livrables Méthodes avant la mobilisation.
 5. Pendant l'exécution du chantier
 Agir comme mentor et conseiller auprès des PMCC sur les enjeux rencontrés pendant l'exécution des chantiers.
 Fournir des recommandations sur la gestion des risques, des écarts budgétaires et des problématiques contractuelles.
 Promouvoir les meilleures pratiques en matière de sécurité, qualité, livraison et coûts.
 Faciliter le partage d'expérience sur la coordination entre les équipes de chantier, Engineering et Supply Chain.
 Effectuer des visites de chantier ponctuelles afin de partager son expertise et de soutenir les équipes, au besoin.
 6. Mise en service
 Conseiller les PMCC sur la préparation et la coordination des activités de mise en service.
 Partager les meilleures pratiques concernant la planification, le contrôle budgétaire et les exigences documentaires.
 Apporter son expertise sur les interfaces entre construction et mise en service.
 7. SSE et qualité
 Promouvoir une forte culture SSE (santé, sécurité et environnment) et qualité à travers le mentorat et le partage des meilleures pratiques.
 Conseiller sur l'intégration des exigences EHS dans les SoW et les contrats de sous-traitance.
 Encourager l'identification proactive des risques et l'application des standards de sécurité GEV.
 8. Gouvernance et amélioration continue
 Agir comme référent métier et soutenir le développement des compétences des PMCC.
 Contribuer à l'amélioration des processus, outils et méthodes de gestion de projet C&C.
 Faciliter le partage des Lessons Learned après les phases majeures des projets (Démontage, Montage, Mise en service).
 Conseiller les Directeurs de Projet et les PMCC sur les situations complexes nécessitant une expertise senior.

 GameSim est un studio de développement vidéoludique qui collabore avec des clients afin de créer des jeux aux styles artistiques variés, que ce soit sur PC ou sur console.  Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) artiste en chef en environnements pour aider à définir et à améliorer la qualité, l’efficacité et la cohérence de la production artistique environnementale à travers les projets GameSim.
 Il s’agit d’un poste de collaborateur(-trice) individuel(le) senior de haut niveau pour un(e) artiste expérimenté(e) capable d’œuvrer tant au niveau stratégique qu’opérationnel. Vous effectuerez un travail de qualité exemplaire, établirez des normes de production pratiques, résoudrez des problèmes artistiques et techniques complexes, et guiderez les équipes en environnements travaillant sur différents projets, moteurs, styles et studios partenaires.
 Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les directeurs artistiques, les gestionnaires de projet, les équipes d’art technique, de production, de conception et d’ingénierie, les clients et les studios partenaires pour traduire des objectifs créatifs en stratégies claires et réalisables pour l’art des environnements.
 Ce rôle exige une grande capacité de leadership, un esprit critique, une aptitude à communiquer clairement, et la capacité à influencer les équipes par l’expertise, l’exemple et la collaboration.
 Définition du succès
 Au cours de vos 90 premiers jours de travail…
 vous développerez une solide compréhension des projets, des clients, de la structure de production et des capacités en matière d’art des environnements de GameSim;
 vous bâtirez une relation de confiance avec les artistes, les responsables de projet, les clients et les studios partenaires grâce à une communication claire et à une prise de décision fiable;
 vous créerez ou guiderez le développement d’un travail de qualité exemplaire qui établit un niveau visuel et technique clair;
 vous identifierez un défi artistique, technique ou lié aux flux des travaux significatif, et contribuerez à la mise en œuvre d’une amélioration concrète;
 vous fournirez des commentaires et du mentorat qui améliorent la qualité, la cohérence et l’efficacité de l’équipe des environnements.

 Exécution et leadership artistique
 Créer des environnements en temps réel de haute qualité, de l’architecture, des kits modulaires, des éléments vedettes, des matériaux, des terrains, de la végétation et du contenu de construction de monde.
 Produire des éléments et des scènes de référence qui communiquent les attentes en matière de composition, d’échelle, de hiérarchie visuelle, de qualité des matériaux, de narration environnementale et de peaufinage final.
 Traduire la direction artistique, l’art conceptuel, les documents de référence, les exigences de conception, les commentaires des clients en objectifs de production clairs.

 Maintenir une contribution pratique significative lors de l’établissement des normes de qualité, de la validation des flux des travaux, de la résolution de problèmes complexes ou du soutien aux livrables essentiels.
 Évaluer objectivement les créations des environnements et fournir des commentaires précis et exploitables par le biais de revues, de corrections graphiques, de maquettes, de planches de référence, de documentation ou d’exemples intégrés au moteur.
 Développement de la production et des pipelines
 Collaborer avec la direction artistique, la production et l’équipe d’art technique pour définir des flux des travaux des environnements qui équilibrent la qualité visuelle, le champ d’application, le calendrier et les exigences techniques.
 Identifier tôt dans le processus les risques artistiques, techniques et de production, et recommander des solutions pratiques.
 Aider les équipes à décomposer des instructions générales ou incomplètes en tâches, étapes, priorités et critères d’acceptation compréhensibles.
 Améliorer les pipelines de création des environnements artistiques grâce à des flux des travaux réutilisables, des modèles, de la documentation, des exemples d’éléments et des normes de production.
 Soutenir la planification et l’estimation en évaluant la complexité des actifs, les dépendances, les besoins en personnel et les risques de production.
 Résoudre les problèmes complexes liés à la construction d’éléments, aux matériaux, à la création des mondes, à l’optimisation, à la mise en œuvre du moteur ou à l’intégration du contenu.

 Influence de l'équipe et du projet
 Guider les artistes en environnements au sein des équipes internes, des studios partenaires et des groupes de développement externes.
 Encadrer les artistes seniors et les responsables en devenir en matière de jugement artistique, de communication, de planification, de pratiques d’évaluation et de prise de décision.

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!




WHY THIS ROLE?

In this role, you will manage the team that owns the Cohere inference APIs and SDKs, as well as the Cohere Dashboard, where customers can access our models, manage teams, and audit billing. You will collaborate with internal partners to craft a delightful, intuitive, and unified experience across everything the Cohere APIs and Cohere Dashboard have to offer. As a hands-on leader, you will shift seamlessly between roles as mentor, strategist, and technologist to guide the team toward shared success.

Join our team of builders who are shaping the future of large language models!




AS AN ENGINEERING MANAGER OF THE COHERE APIS AND DEVEX TEAM, YOU WILL:

 - Manage, mentor, and grow a talented and enthusiastic team of backend and full-stack software engineers

 - Participate in model releases and develop new API capabilities

 - Work closely with Modelling and Model Serving teams

 - Collaborate with UX designers to ensure customers have an easy and delightful time managing teams, API keys, billing and configurations.

 - Oversee and contribute to open source projects

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. We design products that are clear, fast, and dependable - tools that feel human, not overwhelming - so owners can focus on what matters most: their customers and their food.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Vous êtes cuisinier expérimenté et vous rêvez de travailler au Québec ? 
 Un poste où vous n'êtes pas un numéro dans une grosse brigade, et où on vous confie les clés quand le chef n'est pas là. 
 À propos de l'employeur 
 S'installer au Canada, ce n'est pas juste changer de pays. C'est aussi choisir un endroit où on a envie de travailler tous les jours.
 Ici, c'est une auberge-restaurant installée dans une maison ancestrale, sur la Côte-de-Beaupré, face au fleuve Saint-Laurent. Vingt minutes de Québec, dix minutes du Mont-Sainte-Anne. Huit chambres rénovées à l'étage, un restaurant au rez-de-chaussée, et une clientèle fidèle : les gens du coin toute l'année, les touristes venus de France, des États-Unis et du Canada pendant la belle saison.
 On sert entre 35 et 50 couverts sur un service classique, et plus de 100 quand il y a un mariage ou un événement. Le brunch du dimanche est un rendez-vous.
 L'entreprise compte 23 personnes, dont une brigade de cuisine de 5 au maximum. Tout le monde se connaît, et la direction est joignable directement.
 Votre rôle 
 Vous êtes le bras droit du chef. Au quotidien, vous êtes sur la production et la mise en place. Et quand il est en congé, c'est vous qui tenez la cuisine.
 C'est un poste pour quelqu'un de fiable, qui sait travailler vite et proprement, et qui n'a pas besoin qu'on lui dise quoi faire à chaque service.
 Vos missions 
 ● Épauler le chef sur la mise en place et la production.
 ● Assurer les services du soir et le brunch du dimanche.
 ● Remplacer le chef pendant ses congés et garder la cuisine sur les rails.
 ● Travailler les deux cartes de la maison : la cuisine québécoise traditionnelle et la carte contemporaine.
 ● Participer aux services événementiels (mariages, groupes, plus de 100 couverts).
 ● Respecter les normes d'hygiène et de salubrité.
 ● Travailler en bonne intelligence avec la salle.
 Profil recherché 
 ● Vous avez une expérience solide en cuisine et vous savez tenir un service seul.
 ● Vous êtes polyvalent et vous vous adaptez vite à une nouvelle carte.
 ● Vous êtes autonome, organisé et fiable.
 ● Vous aimez les petites équipes.
 ● Vous êtes curieux de la cuisine du terroir québécois.
 ● Vous souhaitez vous installer durablement au Québec.

 ● Poste permanent à temps plein.
 ● Salaire de 23 $ à 25 $ de l'heure selon votre expérience.
 ● Une brigade à taille humaine, sans turnover permanent.
 ● Un rôle de bras droit avec de vraies responsabilités quand le chef n'est pas là.

 Workin Québec vous accompagne de A à Z : 
 ● démarches administratives et permis de travail ;
 ● préparation à votre arrivée ;
 ● accompagnement dans votre installation au Québec.

 ● Une auberge-restaurant de caractère, dans un cadre que peu de cuisines peuvent offrir.
 ● Une petite brigade où votre travail se voit.
 ● Deux cuisines à travailler : le terroir québécois et une carte contemporaine.
 ● Une direction accessible et des décisions rapides.
 ● Un projet d'immigration accompagné de bout en bout par Workin Québec.

 Workin Group est une agence de recrutement internationale spécialisée dans l'expatriation au Canada, basée en France, à Lille, et à Montréal au Canada. 
 L'entreprise accompagne des dizaines de familles chaque année dans leur changement de vie. Grâce à nos expériences et nos expertises, nous accompagnons les futurs expatriés dans toutes leurs étapes.

L’Analyste des systèmes d’affaires (BSA) - Salesforce agit comme un lien entre les besoins d’affaires et la solution technique Salesforce. Il ou elle analyse les processus, définit les exigences fonctionnelles et soutient la mise en œuvre, le maintien et l’amélioration continue des systèmes d’affaires de l’entreprise.

 Recueillir, analyser et documenter les besoins d’affaires et les exigences système avec les parties prenantes.
 Traduire les besoins en exigences fonctionnelles et non fonctionnelles et définir des critères de succès mesurables.
 Analyser et optimiser les processus « as-is » / « to-be » et les modéliser avec BPMN, Visio ou outils similaires.
 Produire et maintenir la documentation d’analyse : BRD, FRD, User Stories, Use Cases, RTM, Fit-Gap, analyses d’impacts, CAB et documentation d’ateliers.

 Gérer la roadmap des produits et solutions et identifier les opportunités d’amélioration continue.
 Coordonner le cycle de vie des applications : maintenance, mises à niveau, fournisseurs, sécurité, performance et améliorations.
 Animer les ateliers, rencontres et comités décisionnels et assurer la collaboration entre les différentes équipes.
 Soutenir l’assurance qualité : plans et cas de tests, UAT, validation des exigences et gestion des anomalies.
 Contribuer aux intégrations système : interfaces, mappage et validation des données, qualité et intégrité des données.
 Soutenir la gestion du changement: analyse d’impacts, préparation, formation et transfert des connaissances.
 Assurer le soutien applicatif N3 et coordonner les escalades N4 avec les fournisseurs et équipes de développement.
 Suivre la performance des solutions, recommander des améliorations et contribuer à la gouvernance et à la création de valeur.
Pour vous joindre à notre équipe: 
 Minimum de 5 ans d'expérience à titre d'analyste d'affaires, d'analyste des systèmes d'affaires ou d'analyste fonctionnel.
 Bilinguisme (français et anglais), à l'oral comme à l'écrit

 Bonne connaissance de Salesforce

 Documentation: Suite Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) et SharePoint

 Méthodologies : Agile, Scrum et Waterfall

 Programme annuel de bourses pour frais de scolarité de l'AIM jusqu'à 8 500 $ par personne à charge admissible
 Les outils et le soutien nécessaires pour réussir dans votre carrière et votre perfectionnement professionnel

veritree & Job Overview
 veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.
veritree is seeking a Head of Carbon to lead the strategic development, build-out, and operations of veritree’s carbon business. Carbon is one of veritree’s fastest-growing new revenue lines, and this role will own the strategic function (project sourcing oversight, technology enablement, strategic partnerships, and sales oversight) working alongside the Carbon Specialist, who conducts project sourcing, day-to-day project relationships, and credit retirement. This role owns the frameworks, pricing, sales engine, and systems that let carbon scale. It is a high-ownership opportunity to grow a business line and shape the future of carbon across veritree. This role reports into Corporate Development and will work cross-functionally with Sales, Product, and Operations to build carbon into a durable, high-margin line of business.
 Key Outcomes:
1 Month Key Outcomes
 Fully ramped on veritree's carbon business (current portfolio, contracts, and 2026 targets) with key relationships built across Sales, Product, and Operations
 Carbon credit resale process and pricing assessed end-to-end; quick wins identified to improve turnaround and margin on the existing portfolio
 Gaps in veritree's carbon storytelling and sales/marketing materials mapped, informing the “charismatic carbon” content plan
 3 Month Key Outcomes
 Carbon growth strategy drafted (including resale enhancement, technology enablement, and strategic partnerships) and reviewed with leadership
 Resale motion improved on the existing carbon credit portfolio, with measurable movement on pricing, partner mix, or process
 V1 of a carbon inventory tracker live and in use by at least one other function (e.g. Sales)
 Delivery of first sales enablement and/or marketing piece(s) of “charismatic carbon” content (project-specific or portfolio-level storytelling) delivered to support Sales
 6 Month Key Outcomes
 A clear carbon growth strategy finalized: strengthening the resale motion on veritree’s existing carbon credits and building out veritree’s “charismatic carbon” narrative (project-specific and portfolio-level storytelling) to support Sales
 Carbon pipeline and inventory fully visible in HubSpot, with forecasting Finance can rely on
 Carbon’s operating model is established end-to-end: portfolio strategy, technology enablement (veritree platform integration, carbon project monitoring functionality built), and 1+ strategic partnership actively progressing, with Carbon Specialist fully supported on day-to-day project relationships and credit retirement
 veritree is on pace to deliver >$500k in 2026 carbon revenue with $750k of 2027 runrate, and a plan is in place for how the carbon function scales into dedicated supply & demand roles
 What You’ll Do:
 Carbon strategy & growth
 Own the strategic roadmap for veritree’s carbon business, setting priorities across sourcing, sales, storytelling, and technology
 Identify and evaluate new revenue opportunities within carbon resale and monitoring (resale channels, new buyer segments, adjacent products)
 Build out veritree’s “charismatic carbon” narrative, partnering with sales and marketing on material that make the case for carbon as more than a compliance product
 Represent carbon in company-wide planning and ensure the function’s targets ladder up to Corporate Development’s goals
 Portfolio development & delivery
 Set the strategy for portfolio construction, working closely with the Carbon Specialist on which project developers and geographies to prioritize
 Provide oversight on due diligence frameworks and scoring systems to ensure a credible, audit-ready portfolio that stands to enhance trust in veritree’s brand
 Identify and execute ways to accelerate the resale of veritree’s carbon credits, including pricing, buyer/reseller partnerships, and process improvements that grow margin and velocity on the existing portfolio
 Sales & inventory
 Build and own a live carbon credit inventory system: what's available, reserved, retired, and priced, so Sales always has accurate numbers to sell against
 Own the carbon sales pipeline and forecast, including how carbon deals move through HubSpot
 Define the process for how Sales and BD reps quote, reserve, and close carbon deals to minimize Carbon team support
 Track margin and velocity by project and by reseller partner
 Technology enablement
 Partner with the Product team to co-own and manage the roadmap for carbon’s technology needs and integration with our tech stack
 Translate and optimize carbon workflows (sourcing, due diligence, resale, retirement) into scalable and repeatable processes aligned with the veritree’s other business lines
 Ensure carbon’s systems and data can support growth into new buyer segments and resale channels
 Team leadership
 Build partnerships that extend veritree’s carbon capabilities (e.g. with carbon project developers or nature-based carbon credit offtakers)
 Act as the reseller lead for larger, more complex carbon transactions
 Provide strategic oversight to the broader carbon team and define how the team’s structure evolves as it scales
 Requirements 
 Professional Requirements or Qualifications
 Bachelor’s degree in Business, Environmental Science, Sustainability, Finance, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
 10+ years of experience in carbon markets, environmental commodities, or a related sustainability/climate business function
 Strong understanding of voluntary carbon market mechanics (project types, verification standards and bodies, and credit issuance/retirement processes)
 Proven track record of structuring partnerships, resale/brokerage deals, or commercial transactions in a new or scaling business line
 Skilled in building the frameworks, scoring systems, and processes that bring discipline to an early-stage function
 Personal Strengths
 Entrepreneurial mindset with a bias toward action and ownership
 Strategic thinker who can operate autonomously in ambiguity and bring structure to a fast-evolving market
 Strong relationship-builder, comfortable engaging project developers, buyers, and internal stakeholders across Sales, Product, and Operations
 Pragmatic and business-minded sustainability professional
 Nice to Haves (not mandatory)
 Certifications like GHG Protocol, Verra VCS, or similar carbon market credentials are a strong plus
 Experience with carbon project development or MRV (measurement, reporting, verification)
 Familiarity with climate tech platforms or environmental data systems
 Benefits

 Some highlights you can expect include:
 Competitive salary with a performance-driven framework that ensures fair and consistent compensation reviews, tied to individual impact and business growth
 Extended health, dental, and vision benefits
 Additional Health Spending Account (HSA) / Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) to support your well-being and lifestyle interests
 A variety of time-off programs, including vacation, personal days, and a 4-week remote work program each year
 Employee discount with tentree, our sister company
 A flexible, hybrid work environment designed for collaboration and focus-driven impact

Responsibilities include development of lighting layouts, single-line diagrams, wiring schematics, grounding systems, photometric analyses, and engineering reports while ensuring compliance with applicable codes, regulations, and quality management requirements.

 Prepare and review roadway lighting design packages including layouts, single-line diagrams, wiring schematics, and grounding details.

 Produce technical reports, specifications, tender documentation, and engineering deliverables for infrastructure projects.
 Conduct design reviews to verify accuracy, completeness, and compliance with project requirements and QA/QC procedures.

 Collaborate with multidisciplinary project teams to integrate electrical systems with broader transportation infrastructure works.
 Support regulatory compliance by applying applicable electrical codes, transportation standards, and engineering practices.
 Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior engineers and designers.

 Participate in stakeholder and client coordination meetings to provide technical recommendations and project updates.
Required 
 Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering from an accredited institution.
 Professional Engineer ( P.Eng. ) designation in good standing with a Canadian engineering regulator.
 5-10 years of progressive electrical engineering experience.
 Minimum 3 years of direct roadway lighting design experience.
 Experience designing electrical systems for transportation and infrastructure projects.
 Proficiency with AutoCAD and/or AutoCAD Civil 3D .
 Strong working knowledge of the Canadian Electrical Code (CEC) .
 Experience with O.Reg. 22/04 certification requirements.
 Experience coordinating with utility authorities and external stakeholders.
 Experience preparing engineering calculations, technical documentation, and construction support deliverables.
 Experience using lighting calculation software including AGI32 and/or AutoLux .
 Assets

 Additional experience supporting commissioning, construction inspection, and utility relocation initiatives.
 Exposure to large-scale transportation corridor or municipal infrastructure projects.
 Experience supporting multidisciplinary infrastructure delivery programs.

 · Le soutien aux projets. Nous appuyons les responsables de projet avec le contrôle des coûts, les agents de projet, le contrôle documentaire, la formation et le suivi des risques. 
 · La transformation opérationnelle. Nous faisons évoluer nos processus, nos outils et nos mesures de performance, avec une gouvernance claire, pour améliorer en continu notre façon de gérer les projets. 
 Notre façon de travailler 
 Nous accompagnons chaque projet de bout en bout, de l'offre de service à la clôture. Nous croyons à l'intelligence collective et à la collaboration, avec les valeurs de Norda Stelo : confiance, excellence, intégrité, respect, innovation et adaptabilité. 
 Notre ambition 
 Être le partenaire privilégié de nos équipes de vente et de projet : des offres de service mieux préparées pour remporter des mandats rentables, et des projets mieux soutenus pour les livrer avec confiance. 
 Votre rôle : influencer, anticiper et faire évoluer 
 Relevant de la Directrice du Bureau de gestion de projet, vous serez responsable de la gouvernance financière et de la fiabilité des données de performance pour l'ensemble du portefeuille de projets. 
 Vous agirez comme une référence en contrôle des coûts et un partenaire stratégique auprès des directeurs et responsables de projets. Votre capacité à analyser les résultats, anticiper les risques et formuler des recommandations éclairées contribuera directement à la qualité des décisions et à la performance financière de l'organisation. 
 Au-delà du suivi financier, vous aurez l'occasion de structurer, d'harmoniser et de faire évoluer les pratiques de contrôle des coûts à l'échelle de Norda Stelo. 
 Votre influence ne se limitera pas aux chiffres : elle contribuera à façonner nos façons de gérer et de piloter les projets. 
 Vos principaux mandats et responsabilités 
 Assurer une vision globale de la performance financière : consolider, analyser et interpréter les données financières de l'ensemble du portefeuille afin d'offrir une lecture claire de la santé des projets. 
 Anticiper les risques et les écarts : identifier les tendances, les dépassements potentiels et les enjeux financiers, évaluer leurs impacts et proposer des stratégies d'intervention. 
 Piloter les prévisions financières : superviser les suivis budgétaires, analyser les coûts engagés et les coûts à terminaison, et produire des prévisions consolidées fiables. 
 Conseiller les équipes de direction : accompagner les directeurs et responsables de projets dans l'analyse de leur performance financière et les soutenir dans leurs prises de décision. 
 Optimiser le contrôle des coûts : recommander des mesures correctives, évaluer les impacts financiers des changements de portée et contribuer à la maîtrise des budgets. 
 Faire évoluer les pratiques : développer, harmoniser et améliorer les outils, méthodes et processus de contrôle des coûts à l'échelle de l'organisation. 
 Garantir la qualité de l'information : effectuer des vérifications ciblées afin d'assurer l'exactitude, la cohérence et la fiabilité des données financières et des prévisions. 
 Partager votre expertise : agir comme personne-ressource auprès des équipes, favoriser le transfert de connaissances et contribuer au développement d'une culture de gestion axée sur la rigueur et la performance. 
 Votre profil 
 Baccalauréat ou DEC en finance, comptabilité, administration, ingénierie ou dans un domaine pertinent. 
 10 ans et plus d'expérience en contrôle des coûts, en contrôle de projets ou en analyse financière dans un environnement de projets. 
 Expérience significative dans un environnement d'ingénierie, de construction, industriel ou multidisciplinaire (un atout). 
 Excellente maîtrise du suivi budgétaire, de l'analyse des écarts, des prévisions financières et des estimations à terminaison. 
 Maîtrise avancée d'Excel et aisance avec les systèmes et outils de gestion de projets. 
 Fortes capacités d'analyse, de synthèse et de vulgarisation de l'information financière. 
 Aptitude à influencer, conseiller et mobiliser des intervenants à différents niveaux de l'organisation. 
 Leadership, autonomie, rigueur et esprit d'amélioration continue. 
 Bilinguisme français et anglais, à l'oral comme à l'écrit. 
 La connaissance de la langue anglaise est demandée, car le poste nécessite de transiger avec des clients et collègues anglophones des États-Unis/Ouest canadien. 
 Pourquoi choisir Norda Stelo? 
 Parce qu'ici, votre expertise peut avoir un impact bien au-delà de votre rôle! 
 Une influence à l'échelle de l'organisation : une vision transversale du portefeuille et la possibilité de faire évoluer les pratiques de gestion. 
 Une proximité avec les décideurs : un accès direct à la direction et une contribution concrète aux orientations du Bureau. 
 Une diversité de projets : des mandats stimulants dans les secteurs des mines, de l'énergie, des infrastructures et de l'industrie. 
 Un environnement propice à votre développement : formations, mentorat, plan de développement personnalisé et remboursement des formations et certifications admissibles, notamment le PMP. 
 Une carrière à long terme : un poste permanent au sein d'une firme en croissance qui valorise l'initiative et l'expertise. 
 Une culture sérieusement humaine : un milieu où la collaboration, la transparence, l'autonomie et la reconnaissance font partie de notre quotidien.

Aviso Wealth: 
 At Aviso, we are dedicated to improving the financial well-being of Canadians. As a leading wealth management organization, we are committed to leadership, innovation, partnership, responsibility, and community. Working with talented and energetic professionals who exemplify our values every day, you will quickly notice that our people and dynamic ‘oneaviso’ culture sets us apart. If you are looking for interesting and challenging work, at a company committed to its people, find out more about what Aviso has to offer at www.aviso.ca .
 The Opportunity: 
 We are looking to fill an opening for a Senior Product Manager to join Aviso’s Product Management team and help shape the future of investing for Canadians through a best-in-class wealth advisor platform. 
 Reporting to the Director of Product Management, the Senior Product Manager will lead the Advisor Hub product family and directly own Advisor Hub ACP, which serves advisors at ACP introducing brokers and portfolio management firms. You will also manage and coach three Product Owners who own the other products in the family.
 You will help establish and champion our customer-centric product model: empowered, cross-functional teams that discover meaningful customer and business problems, test solutions early, and deliver value incrementally. Working in a leadership triad with a Product Designer and Tech Lead, you are accountable for product value and business viability; the Product Designer leads on desirability and usability; and the Tech Lead and engineers lead on technical feasibility. Together, you share responsibility for product outcomes and make informed trade-offs rather than treating feature delivery as the goal.
 This is both a hands-on product role and a people leadership role. You will bring a deep understanding of customers, product data and business constraints to the area you own, working with your team to discover solutions that deliver measurable outcomes. Across the product family, you will set direction, guide priorities and coach Product Owners to lead their areas as outcome-oriented product leaders rather than backlog administrators. You will also champion this way of working across Aviso, building trust through evidence, collaboration and incremental results as we continue to adopt the customer-centric product model.
 As one aviso: 
 We Care – You do the right thing for clients, partners and colleagues. You build trusted relationships, champion service excellence, and contribute to a culture where people feel valued and supported
 We Dare –You challenge the status quo with bold ideas and fresh perspectives. You embrace change, seek opportunities to innovate and are comfortable exploring new ways of working
 We Share – You collaborate openly and build meaningful relationships. You seek out diverse perspectives, share your knowledge and work together to help colleagues, clients and partners succeed
 We Deliver – You take ownership of your work, honour your commitments and focus on delivering meaningful results. You hold yourself accountable and continuously look for ways to improve
 What your day looks like: 
 Set product direction and measurable outcomes for the product family with the Director of Product Management; align the areas owned by your Product Owners with customer needs and Aviso’s business priorities
 Lead discovery in your own area and coach Product Owners to work with customers, users, data and stakeholders to understand problems, test assumptions, and evaluate opportunities before committing to solutions
 Partner with the Product Designer and Tech Lead in the leadership triad to explore options and balance value, viability, desirability and feasibility; involve engineers early and make trade-offs together
 Break larger opportunities into small, testable increments; collaborate with the team on a practical release plan, learn from each release, and adapt based on customer behaviour and measurable outcomes rather than feature output alone
 Own prioritization and the product backlog for your area, ensuring stories and other work are clear and ordered for implementation; support your Product Owners in doing the same, without taking ownership of engineering implementation or technical delivery
 Work with partners in compliance, privacy, operations, marketing, finance and technology to understand constraints early, address dependencies and ensure solutions can work for the business
 Manage, coach and develop Product Owners across their product areas, creating clarity on outcomes, strengthening discovery and judgement, and fostering collaborative relationships with design and technology counterparts
 Communicate product direction, evidence, trade-offs and results to stakeholders; advocate for the customer-centric product model, demonstrate its value through incremental wins, and help remove organizational barriers to its adoption
 Stay curious about investor needs, industry trends and the competitive landscape, using those insights to challenge assumptions and identify opportunities for meaningful improvement
 Requirements 
 Your experience and skills: 
 Innovation benefits from diverse perspectives, backgrounds and experiences. We encourage you to apply if you meet most, even if not all, of the following requirements:
 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience
 Significant hands-on experience managing technology-powered products; typically 8+ years of related experience, though equivalent depth and impact are welcome
 Demonstrated understanding of a customer-centric product model and modern product discovery and delivery: identifying opportunities, testing assumptions, working across disciplines, and measuring outcomes. You can explain its value and help an organization adopt it in practice
 Experience setting product direction, defining success measures, prioritizing against customer and business outcomes, and delivering value through small, iterative releases
 Strong customer, analytical and problem-solving skills; ability to combine research, feedback and product data to make sound decisions and communicate trade-offs clearly
 Experience partnering closely with product design, technology leads and engineers; enough technical fluency to understand constraints and collaborate effectively without assuming engineering ownership
 People leadership and coaching skills, with the ability to develop Product Owners who own distinct product areas and work effectively within cross-functional teams.
 Business acumen and the ability to work across functions such as customer experience, finance, sales, marketing, operations, compliance and privacy; financial services experience is an asset
 Strong communication and stakeholder-influence skills, including the ability to build support for new ways of working through evidence, collaboration and visible results
 Understanding of end-to-end customer experience and dependencies across products; comfort with product, analytics and collaboration tools
 Fluent communication skills in English are required and bilingual skills in French are an asset
 Benefits 
 Why Aviso Wealth? 
 At Aviso Wealth, you will find a dynamic and inclusive culture that rewards innovation and celebrates success. 
 Here are a few things that set us apart: 
 Competitive compensation package that rewards and recognizes individual contributions
 Excellent health, dental and insurance benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees
 Generous vacation time, fitness benefit, parental leave top-up options
 Matching contributions to our retirement program
 Commitment to the continuous improvement of our staff through learning & development and an education assistance program
 Regular social events to foster teamwork
 Your Information 
 By submitting your application, you consent to the collection, use, and disclosure of your provided personal information for the purposes of assessing your qualifications and suitability for employment with Aviso. Your information will be handled in accordance with applicable Canadian privacy laws, including the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) and relevant provincial legislation. Your data may be shared with authorized personnel involved in the recruitment process and retained only as long as necessary to fulfill these purposes or as required by law.
 Further information is available on the Privacy link on our Career Page – Privacy Policies 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 Aviso welcomes and encourages applications from all qualified individuals including persons with disabilities. If you require an accommodation, we will work with you to meet your needs in all stages of the hiring process.
 We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.
 No recruiters or agencies, please.
 Company Overview: 
 Aviso is a leading wealth management and investment services provider for the Canadian financial industry, with approximately $145 billion in total assets under administration and management, and over 1,000 employees. We’re building a comprehensive, technology-enabled, client-centric wealth services ecosystem. Our clients include our partners, advisors, and investors. We’re a trusted partner for nearly all credit unions across Canada, in addition to a wide range of portfolio managers, investment dealers, insurance and trust companies, and introducing brokers. Our partners depend on Aviso for specific solutions that give them a competitive edge in a rapidly evolving, highly competitive industry. Our investment dealer and mutual fund dealer and our insurance services support thousands of investment advisors. Our asset manager, NEI Investments, specializes in investing responsibly. Our online brokerage, Qtrade Direct Investing®, empowers self-directed investors, and our fully automated investing service, Qtrade Guided Portfolios®, serves investors who prefer a hands-off approach. Aviso Correspondent Partners provides custodial and carrying broker services to a wide range of firms. We have offices in Toronto, Vancouver, and Montreal. Aviso is backed by the collective strength of our owners: the credit union Centrals, Co-operators/CUMIS, and Desjardins. We’re proud to power businesses that empower investors .
 A career with Aviso means being part of a group of talented, energetic professionals who live their values every day, and belonging to an organization dedicated to your success and career development. If you’re looking for interesting and challenging work, at a company committed to its people, apply to join our team.
 Salary 
 This position is posted with an expected salary range of $120,000 - $135,000 CAD annually. Individual compensation packages are based on various factors unique to each candidate and the requirements of the position.

About Moment Energy 
 Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it. 
 Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone. 
 The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy. 
 Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact. 
 We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale. 
 Now is the moment. Join us. 
 The Opportunity 
 Moment Energy is seeking a Certification Engineering Co-op to support our Certification Engineer in researching, coordinating, and documenting the regulatory requirements that allow our battery energy storage systems to be safely certified and deployed.
 This is a hands-on learning opportunity for an engineering student interested in product safety, electrical systems, battery technology, and industry certification standards. You will work closely with engineering, production, and quality teams at our Megafactory in Surrey while gaining exposure to the certification processes behind commercial-scale energy storage products.
 You'll help organize technical documentation, research applicable standards, track certification activities, and support preparation for testing and compliance reviews. Your work will contribute directly to bringing innovative energy storage products to market.
 Responsibilities and Duties 
 Research and summarize applicable certification standards and regulatory requirements, including CSA, UL, and NFPA standards.
 Support the Certification Engineers in understanding and documenting requirements related to UL 1974, UL 1973, UL 9540, and UL 9540A.
 Review engineering drawings, technical specifications, and product documentation to help identify information required for certification.
 Maintain organized certification documentation, technical records, test reports, and compliance evidence.
 Assist with tracking certification milestones, project timelines, outstanding requirements, and action items.
 Support preparation for certification testing by coordinating documentation, product samples, and technical information.
 Assist with communication and information gathering between engineering, production, quality teams, and external testing laboratories.
 Research certification and regulatory requirements for new markets and energy storage applications.
 Help identify gaps in technical documentation and follow up with relevant engineering teams to obtain outstanding information.
 Contribute to improving internal documentation processes, compliance tracking tools, and certification workflows.
 The Candidate 
 We're looking for an individual who is curious, detail-oriented, and eager to learn how complex electrical products are tested, evaluated, and certified.
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Systems Engineering, or another related engineering discipline.
 Strong research, analytical, and technical documentation skills.
 Ability to review technical information, identify key requirements, and summarize findings clearly.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office or Google Workspace, particularly Excel or Google Sheets.
 Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 High attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
 A proactive approach to problem-solving and willingness to ask questions, seek clarification, and learn from others.
 Comfortable collaborating with cross-functional teams in a fast-paced engineering and manufacturing environment.
 Nice-to-Have Experience 
 Previous co-op, internship, or academic project experience involving electrical systems, batteries, or hardware products.
 Familiarity with technical standards, regulatory requirements, or product safety testing.
 Exposure to lithium-ion battery technology or battery energy storage systems.
 Experience reviewing engineering drawings, technical specifications, or test documentation.
 Familiarity with UL, CSA, NFPA, or other North American certification standards.
 Moment Energy Co-op Benefits Highlights 
 Paid Time Off: Co-op’s receive three paid days off per term 
 Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga and fitness center), and free EV charging on-site. 
 Why join us? 
 Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world. 
 Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world. 
 Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence. 
 Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact. 
 Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more. 
 We're a fast-paced and dynamic team. 
 Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace. 
 Moment Energy Benefits Highlights (full time, permanent employees only) 
 Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program. 
 Comprehensive Health Coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents through Manulife.
 Generous Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off plus a paid company closure between Christmas and New Year's, with a generous paid sick leave.
 Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga/fitness), and free EV charging on-site.
 Company Dinner: Weekly Tuesday dinner provided by Moment Energy. We also have a generous supply of coffee and snacks for the office! 
 Our Commitments 
 Moment Energy is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes, including our work environment. We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+. 
 —--- 
 Our Values 
 Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews. 
 We have 5 core values and 1 foundational pillar (Safety is our Foundation) which lays the groundwork for everything we do. 
 Safety is our Foundation 
 We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations. Safety is not only about procedures—it is about vigilance, responsibility, and speaking up when something does not feel right. 
 Safety is everyone's responsibility. We follow safety protocols, use proper equipment, and continuously improve our systems to prevent risks before they occur. If something is unsafe, we stop work and address it. 
 Safety also means protecting our colleagues, customers, and communities by designing reliable products, maintaining safe workspaces, and ensuring our work is done carefully and responsibly. 
 We’re Building a Greener Future Together:
